tldr: MLAgentBench is a benchmark of 13 ML tasks that evaluates whether language model agents can autonomously conduct ML experimentation. Claude v3 Opus achieves the best average success rate of 37.5%, with performance ranging from 100% on well-established datasets to 0% on recent Kaggle challenges.
contributions: Introduces MLAgentBench, the first benchmark for evaluating agents capable of machine learning experimentation, comprising 13 diverse tasks spanning text, image, tabular, graph, and time-series domains.
Designs an LM-based agent inspired by ReAct with structured thinking components (Reflection, Research Plan, Fact Check, Thought) for interpretable decision-making.
Benchmarks multiple LMs (GPT-4, GPT-4-turbo, Claude v1.0/2.1/3 Opus, Gemini Pro, Mixtral) showing Claude v3 Opus achieves the highest average success rate of 37.5%.
Demonstrates tasks from both canonical datasets (e.g., CIFAR-10) and recent challenges launched after LM pre-training to test generalization and mitigate data contamination.
methods: The authors designed MLAgentBench with 13 ML tasks, each specified by a task description, starter files (data and baseline code), and an evaluator that scores final submissions. An LM-based agent operates in a task-agnostic environment where at each step it produces a rationale (Reflection, Research Plan and Status, Fact Check, Thought) and an action (read/write files, execute Python, or submit). The benchmark uses compound actions like 'Understand File' and 'Edit Script' that wrap LM calls. Agents are evaluated on competence (improving the performance metric by at least 10% over baseline) and efficiency (wall-clock time and token count), across 8 runs per agent with up to 50 actions and 5 hours max time.
results: Claude v3 Opus achieves the best average success rate of 37.5% across all 13 tasks. Performance varies widely: 100% success on well-established tasks like the house-price dataset, but only 0-25% on Kaggle challenges and BabyLM. The agent struggles most on recent challenges and research tasks. There is a general positive progression across model generations within the same family (e.g., Claude v1.0 < v2.1 < v3 Opus). GPT-4 obtains notably lower performance than Claude v3 Opus. Out-of-distribution recent Kaggle challenges, potentially unseen during pre-training, present significant difficulty.
limitations: Success rates vary considerably across tasks, from 100% down to 0%, indicating agents still struggle with novel and complex challenges.
Agents face difficulties with long-term planning over many iterations.
Hallucination is a key problem, e.g., models may claim improvement after modifying code without actually executing it.
Performance drops significantly on recent Kaggle challenges and research tasks (e.g., BabyLM, CLRS) that may be outside pre-training data.
Even the best agent only achieves 37.5% average success, indicating substantial room for improvement before reliable autonomous ML experimentation.
